note: Codified from the City of Killeen, TX Code of Ordinances, Chapter 31 (Zoning), Article IV (District Regulations). Primary source is Municode (https://library.municode.com/tx/killeen/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH31ZO), but Municode's own page returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt this session (bot-blocked, consistent with the known Municode issue for some TX cities); the eLaws mirror at killeen-tx.elaws.us rendered successfully and its section text was read directly (raw HTML, not just an LLM summary) for every field except SF-2 max_height_ft (see field note). eLaws does not display a page-level 'current through' supplement/currency date the way Municode does, so the only dates available are the per-section ordinance-amendment citations quoted in each field below; no chapter-wide codification date could be verified. Five conventional single-family districts are codified: A-R1 (Div. 3, Agricultural Single-Family Residential), SR-1 (Div. 3A, Suburban Residential Single-Family), SR-2 (Div. 3B, Suburban Residential Single-Family), R-1 (Div. 4, Single-Family Residential — the district explicitly named in the pre-existing 'SETBACK TABLE OWED' code comment at lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts line 435), and SF-2 (Div. 4A, Single-Family Residential). EXCLUDED: RM-1 (Div. 5, Residential Modular Home Single-Family) because its Area/Height sections could not be retrieved this session (eLaws connection reset on every retry) and no value for it is asserted; RT-1 (Div. 6, Residential Townhouse Single-Family) because it is a zero-lot-line/attached-unit district structurally unlike the conventional detached-lot districts modeled here, matching how peer files in this corpus exclude townhouse/zero-lot-line districts (e.g. new-braunfels-tx.json excludes TH-A/ZH-A). MODELING NOTES: (1) None of the five districts' Area or Height regulation sections state a maximum building lot-coverage or impervious-cover percentage, so max_lot_coverage_pct and max_impervious_pct are not_specified for all five and carry 100 as non-binding stand-ins, per this corpus's established convention (see round-rock-tx.json, new-braunfels-tx.json). (2) SR-1 (Sec. 31-181) states side yards as 'a minimum of twenty (20) feet between structures on adjacent lots, with a minimum side yard of ten (10) feet' — the per-side operative minimum (10 ft) is codified as side_ft; two adjacent 10-ft side yards sum to the stated 20-ft between-structures figure, so this is read as one consistent rule, not an additional constraint. Sec. 31-181 states no distinct corner/street-side value for SR-1, so side_corner_ft mirrors side_ft (10) and is flagged not_specified. (3) SR-2 (Sec. 31-185.3) states height only as 'in excess of three (3) stories' with no feet value anywhere in the section — converting stories to feet would be fabrication, so max_height_ft is not_specified for SR-2 and carries 100 as a non-binding stand-in, per the same convention used for round-rock-tx.json and taylor-tx.json. (4) R-1 (Sec. 31-188) states the rear yard depth 'measured from the centerline of the easement as in the subdivision ordinance' rather than from the rear lot line — this is a different measurement basis than the other four districts (and than most peer cities in this corpus) and is flagged here so a consumer does not treat the 25-ft R-1 rear figure as directly comparable to a from-lot-line rear setback. (5) SF-2 max_height_ft (Sec. 31-194) could not be read from raw HTML directly (the eLaws connection reset on every retry this session); the value and quote come from a single WebFetch (LLM-summarized) read of the same URL rather than a direct human read of the source markup, so it carries a lower confidence and 'asserted' rather than 'human-verified' state even though a specific ordinance citation is quoted. Every other field on every other district was read directly from the raw eLaws HTML. CORRECTION (2026-09-07, before landing): all atom_did values in this file originally used a fabricated convention (killeen_tx/ch31/<section>, e.g. killeen_tx/ch31/31-174) that did not match this jurisdiction's real code-section atom corpus, which already exists (killeen_tx/killeen-development-regulations-current-supplement/<section>, section numbers hyphenated not dotted, e.g. .../31-185-3 not 31-185.3) -- corrected before landing. Round-tripping every cited section's real bodyText against this file's quotes (not assumed from atom count alone) surfaced two real transcription errors, both now corrected: R-1 (Sec. 31-188) front_ft was coded 25 ft, quoted as 'twenty-five (25) feet' -- the real ordinance text reads 'not less than twenty (20) feet'; R-1 side_ft was coded 7 ft, quoted as 'seven (7) feet' -- the real text reads 'not less than five (5) feet'. SF-2 (Sec. 31-195) front_ft was coded 25 ft, quoted as 'twenty-five (25) feet' -- the real text reads 'not less than twenty (20) feet'. All three corrected to match the verbatim real ordinance text, verification_state upgraded to human-verified (each is now a real, confirmed atom-corpus round trip). Every other field in this file was independently re-verified against the real atom bodyText and matched the original quote exactly (including SF-2 max_height_ft, upgraded from asserted to human-verified since the real atom now confirms it directly, and SR-2's height not_specified treatment, confirmed the real section genuinely states no feet value). SR-1/SR-2's district-level Sec. 31-185.3/31-185.4-style citations are the only ones whose section_number format changed (dot to hyphen) to match the real corpus; no other values changed. Also corrected, typography only (no value changed): the real ordinance's ingested text uses the Unicode vulgar fraction '½' for story counts (e.g. 'two and one-half (2½) stories'), not the spelled-out '(2 1/2)' the original research transcribed -- a byte-for-byte mismatch that blocks the gate's G5 round-trip check even though the underlying max_height_ft VALUE was already correct; quotes updated to the literal real character. R-1's front_ft quote similarly needed 'one (1) street' (matching the real text precisely) in place of 'one street'.
